end of this corrupt world and look forward to the prospect
of a new world. They also and perhaps they above all are
affected by the "sufferings of this present time"
', but-says
Paul-they are not so affected in their innermost being
because their true life is hidden and does not belong to this
world but to the future. And so they know that the "suffer-
ings of this present time are not worth comparing with the
glory that is to be revealed to us"
Naturally this is not an easy panacea for our ills, as though
everyone who is having a bad time here could wait to be
richly compensated in the heavenly glory which shall be.
Only he can be comforted and only he can confess the faith
who has clearly understood that his present life is apparent
and unreal if it is not even now determined and sustained
by that future for which he hopes, and that his present life is
imbued with power and truth only if he wills to be what he
is intended to be, only if he really lives by the inspiration of
the future. What does this mean? It may in some sense be
said that all men live by the inspiration of the future, that
they do not wish to be what they are in fact here and now,
but rather what they hope to become. This is true of all
those who are striving in human affairs after any kind of
goal, whether great or small; whether it be the security of a
profession, or the quiet of family life, whether it be recogni-
tion and honour, whether it be power in economic or
political life, whether it be knowledge or the creative
achievement of the artist. At bottom all these men live in the
strength of what they have not yet, what they feel is yet to
come, the future goal of their hopes and strivings; it is this
which gives their life its true content and inspiring energy.
None of them can say to the passing moment: "Do tarry,
thou art so beautiful." And if perhaps in some moment of
good fortune and bliss we feel inclined to say this, yet it is
only because this moment is an earnest of the future. Now
this means that all life which is aiming to reach a goal is
always only a provisional, unfulfilled and relative existence.
What man wishes essentially to be lies ever ahead of him.
